subject.title: [Security] Session hijacking vulnerability due to predictable sequence IDs in gateway client

question: Should this report be disposed as a false positive because event `seq` values are non-authoritative ordering metadata, or should the reporter first be asked for a PoC that bypasses the authenticated WebSocket boundary?
rationale: Source, protocol, and security-policy evidence contradict the proposed attack, but the protected security labels require an explicit human security-boundary disposition.

options.title: Confirm no-action disposition
options.body: Confirm that authenticated socket state—not event sequence numbers—is the security boundary, then close the report as unsupported by a reproducible bypass.

options.title: Request a boundary-bypass PoC
options.body: Ask for a current-main demonstration that injects an accepted request or event without possessing the authenticated connection, credentials, or device identity.

recommendation.title: Confirm no-action disposition
recommendation.body: Confirm that authenticated socket state—not event sequence numbers—is the security boundary, then close the report as unsupported by a reproducible bypass.

likelyOwner.reason: The history connects this person to the gateway-client package and broader gateway protocol behavior, making them the strongest available routing candidate for the final trust-boundary decision.
